simple.meaning: הֲדַר (hădar) is a Hebrew word meaning “magnificence.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: הֲדַר (H1923) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 4:27, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הֲדַר (H1923) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in הֲדַר (H1923) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: הֲדַר (hădar) / H1923 is traced through Daniel 4:27, Daniel 4:33, Daniel 5:18 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Therefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to you, and break off your sins by righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor. Perhaps there may be a lengthening of your tranquility.”

timeline.evidenceText: Therefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to you, and break off your sins by righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor. Perhaps there may be a lengthening of your tranquility.”

This was fulfilled the same hour on Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven from men, and ate grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky, until his hair had grown like eagles’ feathers, and his nails like birds’ claws.
“You, king, the Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar your father the kingdom, and greatness, and glory, and majesty.
